def-bin-fit-statistics.title: Pearson and deviance statistics
def-bin-fit-statistics.html:
For grouped binomial data yi∼Binomial(mi,πi), i=1,…,N, with fitted probabilities π^i from a model with p parameters, the Pearson statistic and the deviance are X2=∑i=1N(yi−miπ^i)2miπ^i(1−π^i),D=2∑i=1N{yilog⁡yimiπ^i+(mi−yi)log⁡mi−yimi−miπ^i},{#eq-bin-fit-statistics}

with the convention 0log⁡0=0. Both compare the fit with the saturated model that gives each group its own probability.

def-bin-latent.title: Threshold model
def-bin-latent.html: Let ε1,…,εn be independent with common continuous distribution function F, and let 𝛃Yi={1,εi≤x(i)⊤β,0,otherwise. The variable 𝛃x(i)⊤β−εi is the latent response, and Yi records the sign of it.

def-bin-logistic.title: Logistic regression
def-bin-logistic.html:
The logistic regression model for independent Yi∼Binomial(mi,πi) is 𝛃𝛃𝛃logitπi=log⁡πi1−πi=x(i)⊤β,equivalentlyπi=exp⁡(x(i)⊤β)1+exp⁡(x(i)⊤β).{#eq-bin-logistic}

The quantity π/(1−π) is the odds of the event, and the ratio of the odds at two covariate vectors is an odds ratio.

def-bin-residuals.title: Residuals for binomial data
def-bin-residuals.html: With w^i=miπ^i(1−π^i), W^=diag(w^i) and h^i the ith diagonal entry of W^1/2X(X⊤W^X)−1X⊤W^1/2, the Pearson and deviance residuals are ri=yi−miπ^iw^i,di=sign(yi−miπ^i)Di, where Di is the ith summand of the deviance in @eq-bin-fit-statistics. Their standardized forms divide by (1−h^i)1/2.

def-bin-separation.title: Separation and overlap
def-bin-separation.html:
Let X be n×p with rows x(i)⊤, and let si=2yi−1. The data are

  1. completely separated if there is a b≠0 with six(i)⊤b>0 for every i;

  2. quasi-completely separated if they are not completely separated but there is a b≠0 with six(i)⊤b≥0 for every i;

  3. in overlap if b=0 is the only b with six(i)⊤b≥0 at every observation.

A vector b of the kind in (a) or (b) is a separating direction.

eq-bin-conditional.html: 𝛃𝛃exp⁡(xkj∗⊤β)∑j=0Mexp⁡(xkj⊤β),

eq-bin-entropy-deviance.html: D=−2∑i=1n{π^ilog⁡π^i+(1−π^i)log⁡(1−π^i)}.

eq-bin-firth-score.html: 𝛃𝛑𝛑∂ℓ∗∂β=X⊤{y−π+h∘(121−π)},

eq-bin-fit-statistics.html: X2=∑i=1N(yi−miπ^i)2miπ^i(1−π^i),D=2∑i=1N{yilog⁡yimiπ^i+(mi−yi)log⁡mi−yimi−miπ^i},

eq-bin-logistic.html: 𝛃𝛃𝛃logitπi=log⁡πi1−πi=x(i)⊤β,equivalentlyπi=exp⁡(x(i)⊤β)1+exp⁡(x(i)⊤β).

eq-bin-score.html: 𝛍𝛃𝛃X⊤(y−μ)=0,μi=miπi=miexp⁡(x(i)⊤β)1+exp⁡(x(i)⊤β),

eq-bin-signed-loglik.html: 𝛃𝛃ℓ(β)=∑i=1n{yilog⁡πi+(1−yi)log⁡(1−πi)}=−∑i=1nlog⁡{1+exp⁡(−six(i)⊤β)},

exm-bin-anes.title: Voting intention in the 1996 American election
exm-bin-anes.title_html: Voting intention in the 1996 American election
exm-bin-anes.html:
The 1996 American National Election Studies survey recorded, for 944 respondents, the candidate they expected to vote for (393 said Dole), party identification from strong Democrat (0) to strong Republican (6), age, education on a seven-point scale and household income on a 24-point scale. Fitting @eq-bin-logistic with these four covariates and age in decades gives

term β^j standard error
intercept −5.471 0.619
party identification 1.2188 0.0709
age (decades) 0.1222 0.0714
education 0.0147 0.0771
income 0.0311 0.0210

One step along the party scale multiplies the odds of a Dole vote by e1.2188=3.383; three steps multiply them by 38.72. Dividing by four bounds the effect on the probability by 0.305 per step, and the average marginal effect is 0.100: one step is worth about ten percentage points, averaged over the respondents (Figure 35.1.1).

exm-bin-anes-inference.title: Tests and intervals in the voting model
exm-bin-anes-inference.title_html: Tests and intervals in the voting model
exm-bin-anes-inference.html: In @exm-bin-anes, education has β^=0.0147 with standard error 0.0771; its Wald statistic is 0.036 and so is the likelihood ratio statistic from dropping it, while age has z=1.71 and p=0.087. For the party coefficient the Wald interval is (1.080,1.358) and the profile likelihood interval (1.086,1.364): the log-likelihood is nearly quadratic here. @exm-bin-separated shows what happens when it is not.

exm-bin-case-control.title: A simulated retrospective study
exm-bin-case-control.html:
Take a population of 200000 with a continuous exposure x1∼N(0,1), an independent binary covariate x2, and logitπ=−5+1.2x1+0.8x2. The prevalence is 0.0178, so there are 3565 cases, and fitting the whole population gives α^=−4.959, β^1=1.202, β^2=0.748.

Now take every case and four random controls per case, and fit the same model to those records as if they had been collected prospectively. Averaged over 400 control samples the slopes are recovered, at β^1=1.201 and β^2=0.755, while the intercept averages −2.339 against the predicted α^+log⁡(ρ1/ρ0)=−4.959+2.623=−2.337.

With data generated from a probit model and fitted with a probit link, the population slope is 0.547 while the retrospective samples average 0.719, too large by a factor of 1.31 (Figure 35.5.1).

exm-bin-deviance-sim.title: Three deviances that mean nothing
exm-bin-deviance-sim.html:
Simulate n=200 observations with one covariate and an intercept in three ways: a correct model with a strong slope, a correct model with a weak slope, and a model that leaves a genuine quadratic effect out of the fitted predictor. All three fit two parameters, so n−p=198 and a chi-squared reference would have mean 198 and standard deviation 19.9. Over 2000 replications:

data-generating mechanism mean deviance standard deviation
correct, strong slope 206.8 14.3
correct, weak slope 263.6 7.0
quadratic omitted 252.2 8.5

Two correct models with the same n and p differ by nearly sixty in mean deviance, and the badly misspecified model has a smaller deviance than one of them: no reference distribution can serve all three (Figure 35.4.1).

The survey model of @exm-bin-anes has ungrouped deviance 528.29 on 939 degrees of freedom; dropping every covariate but education gives an obviously wrong model with deviance 1275.16 on 942. Neither number can be referred to a table.

exm-bin-firth.title: The separated subgroup, penalized
exm-bin-firth.html: Applied to @exm-bin-separated, Firth’s method gives β^1=1.362 with standard error 0.708 and intercept −4.049. The Wald statistic is 1.92, short of the conventional threshold, but the interval from inverting the penalized likelihood ratio is (0.364,4.045), which excludes zero comfortably. With thirteen observations and a log-likelihood as asymmetric as Figure 35.3.1 shows, the quadratic approximation behind the Wald statistic is simply not available.

exm-bin-grouped-fit.title: Is the party scale linear on the logit scale?
exm-bin-grouped-fit.title_html: Is the party scale linear on the logit scale?
exm-bin-grouped-fit.html: Collapse the survey of @exm-bin-anes onto its seven party groups, of between 37 and 200 respondents each, and fit logitπ=β0+β1party. The deviance is 12.765 on 5 degrees of freedom (p=0.0257) and the Pearson statistic is 11.899 (p=0.0362). The Pearson residuals locate the misfit: −2.067 at “independent-Democrat”, where the model predicts 0.132 against an observed 0.065, and 2.122 at “independent-Republican”, where it predicts 0.640 against 0.745. The transition across the middle of the scale is sharper than a straight line in the log odds allows, and a quadratic term does not help: the deviance falls only to 12.762, so the misfit is a step, not a curve.

exm-bin-grouping.title: The same fit, two deviances
exm-bin-grouping.html: Fit logitπ=β0+β1(party)+β2(education) to the survey of @exm-bin-anes. The 944 respondents occupy 47 distinct covariate cells. Grouped, the deviance is 45.99 on 44 degrees of freedom; ungrouped, it is 533.34 on 941. The coefficients and their standard errors agree to machine precision.

exm-bin-hosmer.title: The same model, three verdicts
exm-bin-hosmer.html:
For the four-regressor model of @exm-bin-anes:

groups G C^ p
8 8.670 0.193
10 12.232 0.141
12 16.119 0.096

The p-value halves as G goes from 8 to 12, and different software makes different choices about G, about how to break ties in π^i, and about whether to use equal-sized groups or equally spaced cut-points. None of these choices is more principled than any other.

exm-bin-matched.title: Doubling the effect
exm-bin-matched.html: Simulate 3000 matched pairs with one covariate, stratum intercepts drawn from a normal distribution and β=1, keeping only the discordant pairs. The conditional estimate is 0.942 with standard error 0.037. Profiling the unconditional likelihood numerically over the three thousand intercepts gives 1.884, twice that to three decimals as @prp-bin-conditional(c) requires, and about twenty-four standard errors from the truth.

exm-bin-noncollapsible.title: The odds ratio does not collapse
exm-bin-noncollapsible.title_html: The odds ratio does not collapse
exm-bin-noncollapsible.html: Generate a population of 200000 with two independent covariates, x1 standard normal and x2 Bernoulli with probability 0.3, and logitπ=1.0x1+4.0x2, giving a prevalence of 0.638. Fitting both covariates and an intercept recovers the coefficient of x1 as 1.006. Fitting an intercept and x1 alone, and thereby averaging over x2, gives 0.745, a quarter smaller. There is no confounding here: the two covariates are independent by construction, and the marginal and conditional odds ratios simply differ.

exm-bin-quasi.title: An empty cell
exm-bin-quasi.html: Among the 127 respondents with a doctorate, model the vote by party identification as a seven-level factor with the independent-Republican category (PID=4) as baseline, that being the only middle level with both outcomes present. Three levels have no variation at all, and exactly 3 of the six contrasts run off to infinity. The others behave normally: the contrast for weak Democrats is −3.140 with standard error 0.916. The deviance, 53.808, is well defined, because the diverging coefficients drive their own cells’ fitted probabilities to 0 or 1, contributing nothing to it.

exm-bin-separated.title: A separated subgroup
exm-bin-separated.html:
Of the 944 respondents of @exm-bin-anes, 13 reported that their schooling stopped at or before the eighth grade. Among them party identification predicts the intended vote perfectly: the ten at 0, 1 or 2 on the party scale all expected to vote Clinton, the three at 4 or 6 all Dole. The direction b=(−3,1)⊤, the linear predictor party−3, satisfies six(i)⊤b>0 for all thirteen, so the data are completely separated and no maximum likelihood estimate exists.

Asked to fit logitπ=β0+β1party, software stopped at ten iterations reports β^1=8.75 with standard error 29.3; at twenty-five iterations it reports 23.75 with a standard error of order 104. The deviance falls below 10−3 after ten steps and below 10−9 after twenty-five, and the Wald test is nowhere near significant at either stopping point.

Inference is nevertheless possible, from the likelihood ratio. The profile log-likelihood rises to its supremum of zero, so the set of β1 not rejected at the five per cent level is the half-line (0.902,∞): a one-sided interval, correctly reporting that the data bound the effect from below and not from above.

exm-bin-three-links.title: The survey under three links
exm-bin-three-links.html:
Fitting the model of @exm-bin-anes with the three links gives the following coefficients of party identification.

link β^ rescaled by 1.8138 maximized log-likelihood
logit 1.219 — −264.14
probit 0.673 1.221 −265.96
complementary log–log 0.801 — −273.48

The rescaled probit coefficient reproduces the logistic one to two decimals, and the largest difference between the two sets of fitted probabilities is 0.0305. The complementary log–log fit is a different animal: its fitted probabilities differ from the logistic ones by as much as 0.1596, and with equal numbers of parameters AIC prefers the logit by 18.67. Here the choice between symmetric links is immaterial and the choice of an asymmetric one is not (Figure 35.2.1).

exr-bin-auc-limits.title: B3
exr-bin-auc-limits.html: Suppose the covariate is N(μ1,1) among cases and N(μ0,1) among controls. Compute the AUC of the correctly specified logistic model in terms of Δ=μ1−μ0, and find the Δ needed for an AUC of 0.9.

exr-bin-calibration-out-of-sample.title: B2
exr-bin-calibration-out-of-sample.html: Let η^ be fitted on one sample and evaluated on an independent sample from the same population. Show that the calibration slope b has probability limit 1 if the model is correct and 𝛃β^ is consistent, and explain why a value below one indicates overfitting.

exr-bin-canonical.title: A2
exr-bin-canonical.html: Show from @eq-bin-score that a logistic model containing an indicator column for a group reproduces that group’s observed proportion exactly. What follows for a model whose covariates are a full set of indicators for a categorical variable?

exr-bin-cloglog-interval.title: B2
exr-bin-cloglog-interval.html: Follow-up is divided into intervals (tk−1,tk]. Let Yik=1 if subject i has the event in interval k, given that it has not had it before. Show that a proportional hazards model for the underlying continuous time implies 𝛄log⁡{−log⁡(1−Pr(Yik=1))}=αk+x(i)⊤γ with αk=log⁡{Λ0(tk)−Λ0(tk−1)}, and explain how to fit it with ordinary binary regression software.

exr-bin-concavity.title: C1
exr-bin-concavity.html: Prove that 𝛃𝛃ℓ(β)=−∑ilog⁡{1+exp⁡(−six(i)⊤β)}, with si=2yi−1, is concave in 𝛃β, without computing the Hessian.

exr-bin-deviance-bound.title: A1
exr-bin-deviance-bound.html: Use @eq-bin-entropy-deviance to find the largest and smallest possible values of the ungrouped deviance of a logistic fit, and describe the fits that attain them.

exr-bin-efficiency.title: B3
exr-bin-efficiency.html: With n1 cases fixed and n0=Mn1 controls, show that for a single binary exposure and a rare disease the asymptotic variance of the log odds ratio is proportional to 1+1/M, and deduce that there is little gain beyond M=4 or 5.

exr-bin-empirical-logit.title: B2
exr-bin-empirical-logit.html: For grouped data with all mi large, @exr-tr-empirical-logit fits 𝛃β by weighted least squares on the empirical logits ℓi=logit(si/mi) with weights miπ^i(1−π^i). Show that one Fisher scoring step of @prp-bin-irls, started from the fit that reproduces the observed proportions, is exactly that estimate.

exr-bin-firth-2x2.title: B2
exr-bin-firth-2x2.html: Take a 2×2 table with a single binary covariate, coded as an intercept and an indicator. Compute the hi of @prp-bin-firth, and show that Firth’s pseudo-data amount to adding 12 to each of the four cell counts. What is the resulting estimate of the log odds ratio?

exr-bin-gumbel.title: B1
exr-bin-gumbel.html: Verify that F(u)=1−exp⁡(−eu) is a distribution function, and that if ε has this law then Eε=−γ and Varε=π2/6, where γ=0.5772 is Euler’s constant. Deduce the factor that makes a complementary log–log coefficient’s latent scale comparable with a logistic one.

exr-bin-hauck-donner.title: B3
exr-bin-hauck-donner.html: For a single binary covariate with fitted probabilities π^1 and π^0 in groups of sizes m1 and m0, show that as π^1→1, with everything else fixed, the Wald statistic tends to zero while the likelihood ratio statistic increases to a positive limit.

exr-bin-interaction.title: B3
exr-bin-interaction.html: Two binary covariates enter with an interaction: logitπ=β0+β1x1+β2x2+β12x1x2. Show that β12 is the log of a ratio of two odds ratios, and that β12=0 does not make the effect of x1 on the probability scale the same at both levels of x2.

exr-bin-ld50.title: B1
exr-bin-ld50.html: In logitπ=β0+β1x with β1≠0, the level at which π=1/2 is x1/2=−β0/β1 (in bioassay, the median effective dose). Derive the delta-method standard error of x^1/2, and explain why it becomes useless as β^1 approaches zero.

exr-bin-link-family.title: C1
exr-bin-link-family.html: Consider the asymmetric family of Aranda-Ordaz (1981), π=1−(1+αeη)−1/α for α>0. Show that α=1 gives the logistic response function and α→0 the complementary log–log one. Explain how to test α=1 with grouped data, and why the test has little power with ungrouped data.

exr-bin-link-symmetry.title: A1
exr-bin-link-symmetry.html: Show that the logit and probit links satisfy g(π)=−g(1−π) while the complementary log–log link does not. Deduce that for the first two, exchanging the labels 0 and 1 merely reverses the sign of every coefficient, and say what the exchange does under the complementary log–log link.

exr-bin-matched-2x2.title: B2
exr-bin-matched-2x2.html: For matched pairs with a single binary exposure, let n10 be the number of pairs with an exposed case and unexposed control and n01 the reverse. Show that the conditional estimate of the log odds ratio is log⁡(n10/n01), and that the conditional test of β=0 is a binomial test of 1/2 in n10+n01 trials.

exr-bin-noncollapsible-normal.title: C1
exr-bin-noncollapsible-normal.html: Let logitPr(Y=1∣X,Z)=βX+γZ with Z independent of X. Show that Pr(Y=1∣X) is not of the form logit−1(β∗X), and explain why the best logistic approximation has |β∗|<|β|. What happens as γ→0?

exr-bin-odds-arithmetic.title: A1
exr-bin-odds-arithmetic.html: A logistic model has β^=0.7 for a binary treatment indicator. Give the estimated odds ratio, the divide-by-four bound on the change in probability, and the actual change when the control probability is 0.5, 0.1 and 0.01.

exr-bin-pearson-identity.title: B1
exr-bin-pearson-identity.html: Show that for ungrouped data X2=∑i{yi/π^i+(1−yi)/(1−π^i)}−n, and deduce that for the intercept-only model X2=n exactly, whatever the data. What does that say about X2 as a test of fit?

exr-bin-prevalence.title: A1
exr-bin-prevalence.html: A case–control study has 200 cases and 600 controls, and the disease affects 2% of the population. The fitted intercept is −0.8. Estimate the population intercept, and the probability of disease at the reference covariate values.

exr-bin-ridge-exists.title: B1
exr-bin-ridge-exists.html: Show that for any data and any λ>0 the function 𝛃𝛃𝛃β↦ℓ(β)−12λ‖β‖2 has exactly one maximizer, without assuming rank(X)=p. Show also that if rank(X)=p and both outcomes occur the same is true when the intercept is left unpenalized.

exr-bin-selection-on-x.title: B1
exr-bin-selection-on-x.html: Suppose Pr(S=1∣Y=y,X=x)=ρyg(x) for some g with values in (0,1]. Show that @thm-bin-casecontrol(a) still holds. Then suppose instead that cases are sampled at rate 𝛄ρ1ex⊤γ while controls are sampled at a rate free of x; find the bias in the estimated slopes.

exr-bin-separation-cell.title: A1
exr-bin-separation-cell.html: A model contains an indicator for one level of a categorical covariate, and every observation at that level has yi=1. Exhibit a separating direction, say which of the three cases of @def-bin-separation holds, and describe the fit.

exr-bin-separation-high-dimensional.title: C1
exr-bin-separation-high-dimensional.html: Suppose the rows x(i) are independent draws from a distribution symmetric about the origin in Rp and the responses are independent coin flips. Cover’s counting argument gives the probability of complete separation as 21−n∑k=0p−1(n−1k). Deduce that separation is almost certain when n<2p and almost impossible when n≫2p, and relate this to Chapter 28.

prp-bin-auc.title: What the area under the ROC curve is, and is not
prp-bin-auc.title_html: What the area under the ROC curve is, and is not
prp-bin-auc.html: Let s^i be any scores, let I be a uniformly chosen index with yI=1 and J an independent uniformly chosen index with yJ=0. The area under the curve traced by (false positive rate, true positive rate) as a threshold moves through the scores equals AUC=Pr(s^I>s^J)+12Pr(s^I=s^J), the normalized Mann–Whitney statistic. Consequently the AUC depends on the scores only through their ranks, so it is unchanged by every strictly increasing transformation of s^, and in particular it says nothing whatever about calibration.

prp-bin-calibration.title: In-sample calibration is automatic
prp-bin-calibration.html: Let 𝛃β^ solve @eq-bin-score with 1∈C(X), let 𝛃η^i=x(i)⊤β^, and suppose η^ is not constant. Fit the two-parameter logistic model logitπi=a+bη^i to the same responses. Then a^=0 and b^=1 exactly.

prp-bin-conditional.title: Conditional logistic regression
prp-bin-conditional.html:
In the model above, suppose exactly one member of each set is a case, and condition on that fact. Then:

  1. the conditional probability that member j∗ of set k is the case, given the covariates of the set and that exactly one member is, is 𝛃𝛃exp⁡(xkj∗⊤β)∑j=0Mexp⁡(xkj⊤β),{#eq-bin-conditional}

    free of αk;

  2. the product of these over k is the conditional likelihood; maximizing it gives a consistent, asymptotically normal estimate of 𝛃β as K→∞ with M fixed, and the ordinary inverse-information standard errors apply to it;

  3. for M=1 (matched pairs), let dk=xk1−xk0 be the case-minus-control difference in a discordant pair. The conditional log-likelihood is 𝛃−∑klog⁡{1+exp⁡(−β⊤dk)}, while the profile log-likelihood obtained by maximizing the unconditional likelihood over the αk is 𝛃−2∑klog⁡{1+exp⁡(−12β⊤dk)}. Consequently the unconditional estimate is exactly twice the conditional one, and converges to 𝛃2β.

prp-bin-firth.title: Firth’s modified score
prp-bin-firth.html:
For ungrouped logistic regression with rank(X)=p, let 𝛃𝛃ℓ∗(β)=ℓ(β)+12log⁡det(X⊤WX) with W=diag{πi(1−πi)}. Let hi=πi(1−πi)x(i)⊤(X⊤WX)−1x(i) be the ith diagonal entry of the weighted hat matrix W1/2X(X⊤WX)−1X⊤W1/2. Then 𝛃𝛑𝛑∂ℓ∗∂β=X⊤{y−π+h∘(121−π)},{#eq-bin-firth-score}

where ∘ is the entrywise product. Equivalently, the Firth estimate is a fixed point: it is the ordinary maximum likelihood estimate for pseudo-data in which observation i has yi+hi/2 successes out of 1+hi trials, with hi evaluated at that same estimate. Along any ray tb that completely separates the data, ℓ∗(tb)→−∞.

prp-bin-fit.title: What the two statistics measure
prp-bin-fit.html:
1. (Grouped data.) Fix N and the model, let mi→∞ for every i with πi bounded away from 0 and 1, and suppose the model holds. Then X2 and D both converge in distribution to χ2(N−p), and X2−D→0 in probability.

  2. (Ungrouped data, canonical link.) If mi=1 for every i and 𝛃β^ solves the logistic likelihood equations @eq-bin-score, then D=−2∑i=1n{π^ilog⁡π^i+(1−π^i)log⁡(1−π^i)}.{#eq-bin-entropy-deviance}

    The deviance is therefore a function of the fitted probabilities alone: it does not depend on which observations were successes, it is bounded above by 2nlog⁡2, and it has no χ2(n−p) limit.

  3. (Differences.) For nested models ω⊂Ω with q parameters between them, Dω−DΩ does not depend on the grouping and converges to χ2(q) under the smaller model, grouped or not.

prp-bin-grouping.title: Grouping
prp-bin-grouping.html:
Let y be ungrouped binary data, and suppose the rows of X take N distinct values x(1)∗,…,x(N)∗, the kth occurring mk times with sk successes. Then:

  1. the two log-likelihoods differ by a constant free of 𝛃β, so they have the same maximizers, the same score, the same information and the same likelihood ratio statistics;

  2. the two deviances of @def-glm-deviance differ by −2ℓsat, where ℓsat=∑k{sklog⁡(sk/mk)+(mk−sk)log⁡(1−sk/mk)} is the maximized log-likelihood of the grouped saturated model;

  3. if 1∈C(X), then ∑imiπ^i=∑iyi in either form: the fit reproduces the total number of successes.

prp-bin-interpretation.title: Three readings of a logistic coefficient
prp-bin-interpretation.title_html: Three readings of a logistic coefficient
prp-bin-interpretation.html:
In @eq-bin-logistic, write 𝛃ηi=x(i)⊤β and let xj be a covariate that appears in the linear predictor only through its own coefficient βj. Then:

  1. increasing xj by c with the other covariates unchanged multiplies the odds by ecβj, whatever the values of the other covariates;

  2. ∂π/∂xj=βjπ(1−π), so |∂π/∂xj|≤|βj|/4, with equality exactly at π=1/2;

  3. the average of that derivative over the sample, n−1∑iβjπ^i(1−π^i), is the average marginal effect: the mean change in fitted probability per unit of xj.

prp-bin-irls.title: Fisher scoring for logistic regression
prp-bin-irls.html: For @eq-bin-logistic the Fisher scoring step from b is the weighted least squares fit of the working response z on X with weights W, where wi=miπi(1−πi),zi=ηi+yi−miπimiπi(1−πi), both evaluated at b. The observed and expected information coincide and equal X⊤WX; the log-likelihood is concave in 𝛃β, and strictly concave when rank(X)=p and 0<πi<1.

prp-bin-latent-scale.title: Scale is not identified
prp-bin-latent-scale.html: In @def-bin-latent, replace εi by σεi+τ with σ>0, and 𝛃β by 𝛃σβ+τe1, where e1 picks out an intercept column. The observed responses have exactly the same distribution. Consequently 𝛃β is identified only up to the location and scale of the latent errors, while ratios βj/βk of coefficients of non-intercept covariates are identified.

prp-bin-links.title: Three links and where they come from
prp-bin-links.title_html: Three links and where they come from
prp-bin-links.html:
In @def-bin-latent:

  1. if F is the standard logistic distribution function F(u)=eu/(1+eu), the model is @eq-bin-logistic; if F=Φ, it is the probit model 𝛃Φ−1(πi)=x(i)⊤β. Both F are symmetric about zero, so both links satisfy g(π)=−g(1−π);

  2. if F(u)=1−exp⁡(−eu), the distribution function of the smallest extreme value law, the model is the complementary log–log model 𝛃log⁡{−log⁡(1−πi)}=x(i)⊤β. This F is not symmetric: π leaves 0 slowly and approaches 1 abruptly. Reflecting it, that is, applying the complementary log–log link to 1−π and changing the sign of 𝛃β, gives the log–log model 𝛃−log⁡{−log⁡πi}=x(i)⊤β, with the two tails exchanged;

  3. suppose a positive lifetime T has hazard function 𝛄λ(t∣x)=λ0(t)exp⁡(x⊤γ), and that Y records whether the event has occurred by a fixed time t0. Then Y follows a complementary log–log model with linear predictor 𝛄log⁡Λ0(t0)+x⊤γ, where Λ0 is the integrated baseline hazard. Moreover, if g is a continuous strictly increasing link with the property that for every c>0 replacing the hazard λ by cλ changes g(π) by a quantity κ(c) depending on c alone, and not on Λ0(t0) or x, then g is an increasing affine function of the complementary log–log link.

thm-bin-casecontrol.title: Retrospective sampling under a logistic model
thm-bin-casecontrol.title_html: Retrospective sampling under a logistic model
thm-bin-casecontrol.html:
Let (X,Y) follow 𝛃logitPr(Y=1∣X=x)=α+x⊤β in the population, and let S∈{0,1} indicate inclusion in the sample, with Pr(S=1∣Y=y,X=x)=ρy∈(0,1],y=0,1, depending on y but not on x. Then:

  1. 𝛃logitPr(Y=1∣X=x,S=1)=α+log⁡(ρ1/ρ0)+x⊤β. The slopes are unchanged; only the intercept moves, and it moves by a constant that does not involve x;

  2. let F be a continuous strictly increasing distribution function, suppose 𝛃Pr(Y=1∣x)=F(α+x⊤β), and suppose that for every ratio r=ρ1/ρ0 in some open interval containing 1 there is a constant c(r) with 𝛃Pr(Y=1∣x,S=1)=F{α+c(r)+x⊤β} for all x. If the linear predictor 𝛃α+x⊤β ranges over an interval J with nonempty interior as x varies, then F(u)={1+e−(au+b)}−1 for every u∈J and some a>0, b: wherever the population identifies it, the link is logistic;

  3. if ρ1 and ρ0 are known, or if the population prevalence π¯=Pr(Y=1) is known and the sample contains n1 cases and n0 controls, then α itself is estimable: in the second case α^=α^S−log⁡{(n1/n0)(1−π¯)/π¯}, where α^S is the intercept fitted to the sample.

thm-bin-separation.title: Existence and uniqueness of the maximum likelihood estimate
thm-bin-separation.title_html: Existence and uniqueness of the maximum likelihood estimate
thm-bin-separation.html:
Let rank(X)=p and let ℓ be the logistic log-likelihood of @eq-bin-signed-loglik. Then:

  1. if the data are completely or quasi-completely separated, ℓ has no maximizer: for every 𝛃β there is a 𝛃β′ with 𝛃𝛃ℓ(β′)>ℓ(β);

  2. under complete separation 𝛃𝛃supβℓ(β)=0, and the supremum is approached along any separating ray 𝛃β=tb, t→∞, with every fitted probability tending to 0 or 1;

  3. if the data are in overlap, ℓ attains its supremum at exactly one 𝛃β^∈Rp, and 𝛃β^ solves @eq-bin-score.
